samples.summary: No test covers the `ok && !res.bytes` branch that now emits `HTTP 200` as the HTTP_ERROR message
samples.evidence: `runFilesDownload` guards `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)` and now routes that through `upstreamErrorJson(res)`, which stamps `message: \`HTTP ${res.status}\``. For a 200 response that carried no bytes this yields the nonsensical `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 200'}}`. The new suite (test/upstream-error.test.ts:435-453) only exercises `ok:false` (`fail(status,data)`), and packages/cli/test/files-download.test.ts only has `ok:true` WITH bytes (lines 99,111,123) and one `ok:false` case (line 133) — nothing drives ok-true/no-bytes, so this newly-shaped output is unverified.
searchedFor: read new download cases in packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts
grep upstreamErrorJson call sites in packages/cli/src

samples.summary: Assertions on `bodies.at(-1)` cannot detect an extra/duplicate error body written to stderr
samples.evidence: Both new parameterised tests filter stderr to parseable JSON and assert only on the LAST entry. If a command printed the raw framework body first and the enveloped one second (or printed two error bodies), the test would still pass. The sibling commander-level suite is stricter (`expect(stderrSpy).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` at line 166); the new suite drops that guarantee, so it verifies 'the last JSON line is right', not 'exactly one, correct error body reached stderr'.

samples.summary: Pre-existing upload error test is vacuous with respect to the enveloping behavior this delta introduces
samples.evidence: `makeClient(false)` supplies `data: { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }` (line 31), and the assertion is `expect(err.join('')).toContain('HTTP_ERROR')` (line 223). Because the stub body is itself already a valid envelope, the assertion holds identically whether `runFilesUpload` forwards `res.data` verbatim (old code) or synthesises the HTTP_ERROR envelope (new code) — it can never fail on this behavior. The delta changes the code path this test nominally guards without strengthening it; the real coverage lives only in the new suite.
